bug_semantics: DevSpace's UI HTTP server (default port 8090) exposes gorilla/websocket endpoints that share a package-level Upgrader whose CheckOrigin always returns true. A victim running `devspace ui` who then visits a malicious site can have that site open a cross-origin WebSocket to ws://127.0.0.1:8090 and invoke /api/logs (pod log stream), /api/enter (interactive pod shell), and /api/command (pipeline command execution) with no origin or auth gate. gorilla/websocket's nil-CheckOrigin default is checkSameOrigin; the flaw is the explicit always-true override, not the library default.
flaw_origin: On 2019-10-18, commit 764fefcd27f740c7ca931a4b8079325ab1b9de19 ('Add xterm') replaced `var upgrader = websocket.Upgrader{}` in pkg/devspace/server/logs.go with `CheckOrigin: func(r *http.Request) bool { return true }`. The immediate parent still used the empty Upgrader (nil CheckOrigin → checkSameOrigin). That first write of the always-true origin check is the CSWSH mechanism; later enter/command handlers only reused the same global upgrader.

The commit is not a move, refactor, revert, backport, release, or squash. Shared upgrader reuse by /api/enter and /api/command expanded impact but did not introduce the origin bypass. The override is present at tagged v6.3.20 and replaced in 6b5073d, which is an ancestor of v6.3.21 and not of v6.3.20, matching the patched boundary (CVE: < 6.3.21; GHSA package range lists only 6.3.20 as the last affected release).
